newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds trickle lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds trickle lower in thin trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slipped into negative territory in thin, directional trade Monday.
"It's Monday, there are no economic numbers and nothing is going on," one New York trader said. "It's one of those quiet days," he said.
Pass-throughs were flat to 1/32 lower at 1556 EST/2056 GMT, while comparable Treasuries were off 2/32 to 3/32.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was unchanged from Friday's close at 99-19/32, yielding 100 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were both off 1/32 at 99-17/32 and 99-22/32, respectively.
Despite Monday's sluggish trading session, market players said they have not changed their outlook for pass-throughs, which have been performing relatively well this year.
"Pass-throughs look cheap relative to what is out there," one trader said. "There continues to be pretty decent bid and I think supply is going to be down," he said.
However, the trader said, the caveat for mortgages is volatility.
"Volatility is high ... That doesn't help the market," he said.
Other mortgage experts said the market will not be looking at Tuesday's economic data -- December consumer prices and retail sales -- with any great anticipation.
"They'll be looking for confirmation of what they already know," a trader said. "I don't there is anyone really excited about tomorrow's numbers."
